import Catalog.Applications.PosetTheory.ReflectiveTypeTheory

/-!
# Set-theoretic semantics of reflective propositions, and the positivity guard

The syntax of reflective propositions admits an unrestricted fixed-point binder.  This
file supplies the promised semantics and delimits it.

* `interp` interprets a reflective proposition over a frame: products are intersections,
  function spaces are classical implications, the reflection former is the provability
  operator of the frame, and the fixed-point former is interpreted by the
  Knaster–Tarski candidate `⋂₀ {S | body S ⊆ S}`.
* `PolarityOk` is the usual polarity discipline: implication flips polarity in its
  antecedent, every other constructor preserves it.
* `interp_update_subset` proves that a variable occurring only positively induces a
  monotone operator, and one occurring only negatively induces an antitone one.
* `interp_fix_isLeast` is Knaster–Tarski for guarded codes: the interpretation of
  `fix A` really is the least fixed point of the operator induced by `A`.
* `interp_fix_negVarBody_not_fixedPoint` refutes the unguarded case: the code
  `μX. (X → ⊥)` induces set complementation, which on a nonempty frame has no fixed
  point at all, so its interpretation is not a fixed point of its own body.
* `interp_fix_proof_bound_chain` computes a concrete guarded example: on the three-state
  chain the code `μX. □X` denotes every state.
-/

namespace ReflectiveTypeTheory

open Set

universe u v

variable {Atom : Type v} {F : Frame.{u}}

/-! ## Environments -/

/-- Extend an environment of fixed-point variables with a new binding at index `0`. -/
def consEnv (S : Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) : Nat → Set F.World
  | 0 => S
  | n + 1 => ρ n

@[simp] theorem consEnv_zero (S : Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    consEnv S ρ 0 = S := rfl

@[simp] theorem consEnv_succ (S : Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) (n : Nat) :
    consEnv S ρ (n + 1) = ρ n := rfl

/-- Rebinding index `0` of an extended environment is the same as extending with the new
value. -/
theorem consEnv_eq_update (S U : Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    consEnv S ρ = Function.update (consEnv U ρ) 0 S := by
  funext m
  cases m with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k => simp [consEnv, Function.update]

/-- Extending an environment commutes with rebinding, with the index shifted by one. -/
theorem consEnv_update (S U : Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) (n : Nat) :
    consEnv U (Function.update ρ n S) = Function.update (consEnv U ρ) (n + 1) S := by
  funext m
  cases m with
  | zero => simp [consEnv, Function.update]
  | succ k => simp [consEnv, Function.update]

/-! ## Interpretation -/

/-- Interpretation of a reflective proposition over a frame, relative to a valuation of
the atoms and an environment for the fixed-point variables. -/
def interp (val : Atom → Set F.World) :
    RType Atom → (Nat → Set F.World) → Set F.World
  | .atom a, _ => val a
  | .bound n, ρ => ρ n
  | .empty, _ => ∅
  | .unit, _ => Set.univ
  | .prod A B, ρ => interp val A ρ ∩ interp val B ρ
  | .arr A B, ρ => (interp val A ρ)ᶜ ∪ interp val B ρ
  | .proof A, ρ => F.box (interp val A ρ)
  | .fix A, ρ => ⋂₀ {S | interp val A (consEnv S ρ) ⊆ S}

@[simp] theorem interp_atom (val : Atom → Set F.World) (a : Atom) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.atom a) ρ = val a := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_bound (val : Atom → Set F.World) (n : Nat) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.bound n) ρ = ρ n := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_empty (val : Atom → Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.empty : RType Atom) ρ = (∅ : Set F.World) := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_unit (val : Atom → Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.unit : RType Atom) ρ = (Set.univ : Set F.World) := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_prod (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A B : RType Atom)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.prod A B) ρ = interp val A ρ ∩ interp val B ρ := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_arr (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A B : RType Atom)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.arr A B) ρ = (interp val A ρ)ᶜ ∪ interp val B ρ := rfl

@[simp] theorem interp_proof (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A : RType Atom)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.proof A) ρ = F.box (interp val A ρ) := rfl

theorem interp_fix (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A : RType Atom) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.fix A) ρ = ⋂₀ {S | interp val A (consEnv S ρ) ⊆ S} := rfl

/-! ## Polarity -/

/-- `PolarityOk b n A` says that the fixed-point variable with de Bruijn index `n` occurs
in `A` only with polarity `b`.  Implication flips the polarity of its antecedent; every
other constructor preserves it, and the binder shifts the index. -/
def PolarityOk : Bool → Nat → RType Atom → Prop
  | _, _, .atom _ => True
  | b, n, .bound m => m = n → b = true
  | _, _, .empty => True
  | _, _, .unit => True
  | b, n, .prod A B => PolarityOk b n A ∧ PolarityOk b n B
  | b, n, .arr A B => PolarityOk (!b) n A ∧ PolarityOk b n B
  | b, n, .proof A => PolarityOk b n A
  | b, n, .fix A => PolarityOk b (n + 1) A

/-- A code is *guarded* when its bound variable occurs only positively in the body. -/
def Guarded (A : RType Atom) : Prop := PolarityOk true 0 A

/-! ## Variance: positive occurrences are monotone, negative ones antitone -/

/-- The variance theorem.  Enlarging the value of a variable enlarges the interpretation
when the variable occurs only positively, and shrinks it when the variable occurs only
negatively.  Both halves are proved simultaneously, because function space exchanges
them. -/
theorem interp_update_subset (val : Atom → Set F.World) :
    ∀ (A : RType Atom) (n : Nat) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) (S T : Set F.World), S ⊆ T →
      (PolarityOk true n A →
        interp val A (Function.update ρ n S) ⊆ interp val A (Function.update ρ n T)) ∧
      (PolarityOk false n A →
        interp val A (Function.update ρ n T) ⊆ interp val A (Function.update ρ n S)) := by
  intro A
  induction A with
  | atom a => intro n ρ S T _; exact ⟨fun _ => subset_rfl, fun _ => subset_rfl⟩
  | bound m =>
      intro n ρ S T hST
      by_cases hm : m = n
      · subst hm
        refine ⟨fun _ => ?_, fun hneg => ?_⟩
        · simpa [Function.update] using hST
        · exact absurd (hneg rfl) (by simp)
      · exact ⟨fun _ => by simp [Function.update, hm], fun _ => by simp [Function.update, hm]⟩
  | empty => intro n ρ S T _; exact ⟨fun _ => subset_rfl, fun _ => subset_rfl⟩
  | unit => intro n ρ S T _; exact ⟨fun _ => subset_rfl, fun _ => subset_rfl⟩
  | prod A B ihA ihB =>
      intro n ρ S T hST
      obtain ⟨hAp, hAn⟩ := ihA n ρ S T hST
      obtain ⟨hBp, hBn⟩ := ihB n ρ S T hST
      refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
      · exact Set.inter_subset_inter (hAp h.1) (hBp h.2)
      · exact Set.inter_subset_inter (hAn h.1) (hBn h.2)
  | arr A B ihA ihB =>
      intro n ρ S T hST
      obtain ⟨hAp, hAn⟩ := ihA n ρ S T hST
      obtain ⟨hBp, hBn⟩ := ihB n ρ S T hST
      refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
      · have hA : interp val A (Function.update ρ n T) ⊆ interp val A (Function.update ρ n S) :=
          hAn (by simpa using h.1)
        exact Set.union_subset_union (Set.compl_subset_compl.2 hA) (hBp h.2)
      · have hA : interp val A (Function.update ρ n S) ⊆ interp val A (Function.update ρ n T) :=
          hAp (by simpa using h.1)
        exact Set.union_subset_union (Set.compl_subset_compl.2 hA) (hBn h.2)
  | proof A ih =>
      intro n ρ S T hST
      obtain ⟨hp, hn⟩ := ih n ρ S T hST
      exact ⟨fun h => box_mono F (hp h), fun h => box_mono F (hn h)⟩
  | fix A ih =>
      intro n ρ S T hST
      refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
      · refine Set.sInter_subset_sInter ?_
        intro U hU
        have hstep := (ih (n + 1) (consEnv U ρ) S T hST).1 h
        rw [← consEnv_update, ← consEnv_update] at hstep
        exact fun x hx => hU (hstep hx)
      · refine Set.sInter_subset_sInter ?_
        intro U hU
        have hstep := (ih (n + 1) (consEnv U ρ) S T hST).2 h
        rw [← consEnv_update, ← consEnv_update] at hstep
        exact fun x hx => hU (hstep hx)

/-- A guarded body induces a monotone operator on propositions. -/
theorem monotone_interp_of_guarded (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A : RType Atom)
    (hA : Guarded A) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    Monotone (fun S : Set F.World => interp val A (consEnv S ρ)) := by
  intro S T hST
  have h := (interp_update_subset val A 0 (consEnv (∅ : Set F.World) ρ) S T hST).1 hA
  rwa [← consEnv_eq_update, ← consEnv_eq_update] at h

/-! ## Knaster–Tarski for guarded codes -/

/-- For a guarded code the interpretation of `fix A` is the least fixed point of the
operator induced by `A`: it is a fixed point, and it is contained in every fixed point. -/
theorem interp_fix_isLeast (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A : RType Atom) (hA : Guarded A)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    IsLeast {S : Set F.World | interp val A (consEnv S ρ) = S}
      (interp val (RType.fix A) ρ) := by
  have hmono := monotone_interp_of_guarded val A hA ρ
  set L : Set F.World := interp val (RType.fix A) ρ with hLdef
  have hle : ∀ S : Set F.World, interp val A (consEnv S ρ) ⊆ S → L ⊆ S := by
    intro S hS
    exact Set.sInter_subset_of_mem hS
  have hpre : interp val A (consEnv L ρ) ⊆ L := by
    rw [hLdef, interp_fix]
    refine Set.subset_sInter ?_
    intro S hS
    exact fun x hx => hS (hmono (hle S hS) hx)
  have hpost : L ⊆ interp val A (consEnv L ρ) :=
    hle _ (hmono hpre)
  refine ⟨Set.Subset.antisymm hpre hpost, ?_⟩
  intro S hS
  exact hle S (le_of_eq hS)

/-- In particular, guarded codes are genuine fixed points. -/
theorem interp_fix_eq_of_guarded (val : Atom → Set F.World) (A : RType Atom)
    (hA : Guarded A) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val A (consEnv (interp val (RType.fix A) ρ) ρ) = interp val (RType.fix A) ρ :=
  (interp_fix_isLeast val A hA ρ).1

/-! ## The unguarded case: no fixed point at all -/

/-- The body of the unguarded code `μX. (X → ⊥)`. -/
def negVarBody (Atom : Type v) : RType Atom := RType.arr (RType.bound 0) RType.empty

/-- The bound variable of `μX. (X → ⊥)` occurs negatively, so the code is not guarded. -/
theorem negVarBody_not_guarded : ¬ Guarded (negVarBody Atom) := by
  intro h
  have := h.1 rfl
  simp at this

/-- The operator induced by `X → ⊥` is set complementation. -/
theorem interp_negVarBody (val : Atom → Set F.World) (S : Set F.World)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (negVarBody Atom) (consEnv S ρ) = Sᶜ := by
  simp [negVarBody]

/-- Complementation has no fixed point on a nonempty frame, so the unguarded code
`μX. (X → ⊥)` has no fixed-point semantics whatsoever. -/
theorem negVarBody_no_fixedPoint [Nonempty F.World] (val : Atom → Set F.World)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    ¬ ∃ S : Set F.World, interp val (negVarBody Atom) (consEnv S ρ) = S := by
  rintro ⟨S, hS⟩
  rw [interp_negVarBody] at hS
  obtain ⟨w⟩ := ‹Nonempty F.World›
  by_cases hw : w ∈ S
  · have hc : w ∈ Sᶜ := by rw [hS]; exact hw
    rw [Set.mem_compl_iff] at hc
    exact hc hw
  · have hc : w ∈ Sᶜ := Set.mem_compl hw
    rw [hS] at hc
    exact hw hc

/-- The Knaster–Tarski candidate for the unguarded code evaluates to the whole frame. -/
theorem interp_fix_negVarBody (val : Atom → Set F.World) (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (RType.fix (negVarBody Atom)) ρ = (Set.univ : Set F.World) := by
  refine Set.eq_univ_of_forall ?_
  intro x
  rw [interp_fix]
  refine Set.mem_sInter.2 ?_
  intro S hS
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, interp_negVarBody] at hS
  by_contra hx
  exact hx (hS hx)

/-- Consequently the candidate is not a fixed point: the intended least-fixed-point
semantics fails for unguarded codes.  This is the exact price of dropping positivity. -/
theorem interp_fix_negVarBody_not_fixedPoint [Nonempty F.World] (val : Atom → Set F.World)
    (ρ : Nat → Set F.World) :
    interp val (negVarBody Atom)
        (consEnv (interp val (RType.fix (negVarBody Atom)) ρ) ρ)
      ≠ interp val (RType.fix (negVarBody Atom)) ρ := by
  intro h
  exact negVarBody_no_fixedPoint val ρ ⟨_, h⟩

/-! ## A guarded example computed on the chain -/

/-- The code `μX. □X`, read “provable all the way down”. -/
def wellFoundedCode (Atom : Type v) : RType Atom :=
  RType.fix (RType.proof (RType.bound 0))

/-- Its body is guarded, since the reflection former preserves polarity. -/
theorem wellFounded_body_guarded :
    Guarded (RType.proof (RType.bound 0) : RType Atom) := by
  intro h
  rfl

/-- On the three-state chain every state satisfies `μX. □X`: the accessibility relation is
well founded, so the least fixed point of the provability operator is everything. -/
theorem interp_fix_proof_bound_chain (val : Atom → Set chainFrame.World)
    (ρ : Nat → Set chainFrame.World) :
    interp val (wellFoundedCode Atom) ρ = (Set.univ : Set chainFrame.World) := by
  refine Set.eq_univ_of_forall ?_
  intro x
  rw [wellFoundedCode, interp_fix]
  refine Set.mem_sInter.2 ?_
  intro S hS
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, interp_proof, interp_bound, consEnv_zero] at hS
  have h0 : (0 : Fin 3) ∈ S := by
    refine hS ?_
    intro v hv
    rcases hv with ⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩ <;> exact absurd h (by decide)
  have h1 : (1 : Fin 3) ∈ S := by
    refine hS ?_
    intro v hv
    rcases hv with ⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
    · exact absurd h (by decide)
    · exact h ▸ h0
  have h2 : (2 : Fin 3) ∈ S := by
    refine hS ?_
    intro v hv
    rcases hv with ⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩
    · exact h ▸ h1
    · exact absurd h (by decide)
  suffices hall : ∀ w : Fin 3, w ∈ S from hall x
  intro w
  fin_cases w
  · exact h0
  · exact h1
  · exact h2

/-! ## Sanity checks

The hypotheses above are satisfiable, so none of the statements is vacuous. -/

/-- The three-state chain is a nonempty frame. -/
instance : Nonempty chainFrame.World := ⟨(0 : Fin 3)⟩

/-- On the chain, the unguarded code really does fail to denote a fixed point of its own
body, so the refutation applies to a concrete frame. -/
example (val : Bool → Set chainFrame.World) (ρ : Nat → Set chainFrame.World) :
    interp val (negVarBody Bool)
        (consEnv (interp val (RType.fix (negVarBody Bool)) ρ) ρ)
      ≠ interp val (RType.fix (negVarBody Bool)) ρ :=
  interp_fix_negVarBody_not_fixedPoint val ρ

/-- Reflection is interpreted by the provability operator of the frame. -/
example (val : Bool → Set chainFrame.World) (ρ : Nat → Set chainFrame.World) (a : Bool) :
    interp val (RType.proof (RType.atom a)) ρ = chainFrame.box (val a) := rfl

/-- Function space is interpreted classically, so the empty codomain gives a complement. -/
example (val : Bool → Set chainFrame.World) (ρ : Nat → Set chainFrame.World) (a : Bool) :
    interp val (RType.arr (RType.atom a) RType.empty) ρ = (val a)ᶜ := by
  simp

end ReflectiveTypeTheory

# Future directions

1. **Dependent extension.** Extend both grammars with sums, dependent products and
   dependent sums, and re-derive the retraction and the grammar isomorphism. The partial
   decoder gains failure cases; the translation gains binder-aware clauses. The
   interesting question is whether the isomorphism survives contexts, i.e. whether typing
   derivations, and not merely proposition codes, correspond.

2. **Indexed modalities.** Replace the single reflection former by a family of formers
   with separate accessibility relations, and characterise which mixed iteration
   principles hold on which frame classes. The single-modality results proved here are the
   diagonal case of that programme, and the mixed transitivity condition
   (the composite of the two relations being contained in the first) is the natural
   candidate hypothesis.

3. **Guarded transport of semantics.** Isolate the subclass of guarded fixed-point codes,
   prove the monotone-interpretation theorem in full, and establish that the grammar
   isomorphism restricts to a semantics-preserving bijection between guarded reflective
   codes and positive modal fixed-point formulas. This is the precise repair of the
   refuted monotonicity conjecture.

4. **Quantitative minimality.** Every reflection witness contains a two-edge path; a full
   classification of minimal witnesses up to frame isomorphism, separating the cyclic
   two-world case from the loop-free three-world chain, and of the frames on which the
   iteration principle fails for some but not all propositions, would sharpen the
   boundary further.

5. **Rosser refinement of the diagonal theorem.** Weaken the soundness hypothesis of the
   abstract diagonal theory to a consistency-style hypothesis, and identify the minimal
   abstract structure under which a true unprovable sentence is still forced.
